name: PLA / PLA Basic
brands: Bambu PLA Basic, Bambu PLA Matte
plate: Cool Plate, Textured PEI, or Smooth PEI
drying: Usually not needed; 50 °C for 8 h if stringing
enclosure: Open — lid OFF or door open on Bambu (heat creep)
useCases: Prototypes, jigs, drill guides, cosmetic parts, spacers. Softens ~55 °C — never leave in a hot car or near the curing oven.
notes: Default lab material. Easiest to print, stiffest of the commodity plastics, but brittle under impact and creeps under sustained load.

name: PETG / PETG HF
plate: Textured PEI (NEVER smooth PEI without glue — it welds)
drying: 65 °C for 8 h — hygroscopic; dry if stored open > 2 weeks
useCases: Functional robot parts, brackets, covers, outdoor parts, anything needing impact resistance and a little flex.
notes: Workhorse for on-robot parts. Stringier than PLA; enable coasting and dry the spool if wisps appear.

name: TPU 95A (Flexible)
drying: 70 °C for 8–12 h — REQUIRED; wet TPU bubbles and strings badly
useCases: Intake roller wheels, bumper pads, grippers, gaskets, belt guards, vibration dampers.
notes: Do NOT run standard TPU through the AMS (it jams) — external spool holder only, unless using Bambu's 'for AMS' TPU. Disable retraction or keep it tiny.

name: PA-CF (Carbon Fiber Nylon)
plate: Engineering Plate or Textured PEI + glue stick
drying: 80 °C for 12 h — MANDATORY before every print session; store in dry box
useCases: High-strength brackets, gearbox plates, motor mounts, camera mounts — the strongest printable material in the lab.
notes: HARDENED steel nozzle + extruder gears required — CF chews brass nozzles. X1-Carbon/H2D/X2D only. Never print from a spool that has sat out overnight.

name: PC (Polycarbonate)
plate: Engineering Plate or Smooth PEI + glue
enclosure: Enclosed REQUIRED — warps and delaminates in open air
useCases: High-temperature parts, impact-critical guards, electronics mounts near motors, parts that see > 100 °C.
notes: Prints must stay in the heated chamber until fully cooled or layers crack. Watch first layers closely — PC loves to lift at corners.
